tzi.name: Ötzi
tzi.summary: A natural mummy of a man who lived c. 3275–3230 BC, found in 1991 in the Ötztal Alps; Europe's oldest known natural human mummy, likely killed by another person.

tztal-alps.name: Ötztal Alps
tztal-alps.summary: A mountain range in the Central Eastern Alps, in Austria and Italy, where the mummy Ötzi's remains were found.

los-millares.name: Los Millares
los-millares.summary: A Chalcolithic settlement near Almería, Spain, occupied from about 3025 to 2000 BCE and home to roughly 1,000 people; the type site of the Millaran culture.

almer-a.name: Almería
almer-a.summary: City in southeastern Spain founded in 955 by Caliph Abd al-Rahman III, which grew wealthy trading silk, oil, and raisins under Islamic rule.

einkorn.name: Einkorn
einkorn.summary: A wild or domesticated species of wheat, one of the first cereals ever cultivated, with tough husks tightly enclosing its grains.

south-tyrol.name: South Tyrol
south-tyrol.summary: An autonomous, mostly German-speaking province in northern Italy with strong self-government, among the wealthiest regions in the EU.

prehistoric-rock-art-sites-in-the-c-a-va.name: Côa Valley and Siega Verde
prehistoric-rock-art-sites-in-the-c-a-va.summary: A transboundary UNESCO World Heritage Site of prehistoric open-air rock art, located in the Côa Valley in Portugal and at Siega Verde in Spain.
prehistoric-rock-art-sites-in-the-c-a-va.source_title: Prehistoric Rock Art Sites in the Côa Valley and Siega Verde

cardium-pottery.name: Cardium pottery
cardium-pottery.summary: A Neolithic decorative pottery style made by pressing cockle shells into wet clay, giving its name to the 'Cardial culture' that produced and spread it across the western Mediterranean.

liguria.name: Liguria
liguria.summary: A region of north-western Italy, capital Genoa, crossed by the Alps and Apennines and bordering France, Piedmont, Emilia-Romagna and Tuscany.

statue-menhir.name: Statue menhir
statue-menhir.summary: A type of carved Neolithic standing stone bearing a stylised human figure, sometimes showing clothing or weapons.

magdalenian.name: Magdalenian
magdalenian.summary: A Late Upper Paleolithic culture in Western and Central Europe, dated to about 21,000-13,000 years ago, known for reindeer hunting and cave art.

po-valley.name: Po Valley
po-valley.summary: A major lowland plain of northern Italy running about 650 km from the Alps to the Adriatic Sea, home to a third of Italy's population.

veneto.name: Veneto
veneto.summary: A region in northeastern Italy, home to Venice and Verona; part of the Roman Empire, then the Republic of Venice until 1797, later Austrian territory before joining Italy in 1866.

epipalaeolithic.name: Epipalaeolithic
epipalaeolithic.summary: An archaeological period between the Upper Paleolithic and Neolithic, roughly 20,000 to 10,000 BP in the Levant, marked by nomadic hunter-gatherers making small stone tools called microliths.

yamnaya-culture.name: Yamnaya culture
yamnaya-culture.summary: A Copper to early Bronze Age culture of the Pontic–Caspian steppe (3300–2600 BC), known for pit-grave burials under kurgans and often linked to Proto-Indo-European origins.

tavoliere-delle-puglie.name: Tavoliere delle Puglie
tavoliere-delle-puglie.summary: A plain in northern Apulia, southern Italy, once a sea bottom and now the largest Italian plain after the Po Valley, historically classified for sheep farming.

irpinia.name: Irpinia
irpinia.summary: A geographical and cultural region of Southern Italy, roughly matching today's province of Avellino, once home to the ancient Hirpini tribe.

basilicata.name: Basilicata
basilicata.summary: A region of southern Italy, anciently called Lucania, once part of Magna Graecia before passing through Roman, Byzantine, Norman, Aragonese and Spanish rule.

chalcolithic.name: Chalcolithic (Copper Age)
chalcolithic.summary: An archaeological period between the Neolithic and Bronze Age marked by growing use of smelted copper, with evidence of copper smelting from as early as about 5000 BCE in parts of Europe.

beehive-tomb.name: Tholos tomb
beehive-tomb.summary: A burial structure with a false dome built by stacking successively smaller rings of stone or mudbrick, used in several Mediterranean and West Asian cultures.

remedello-culture.name: Remedello culture
remedello-culture.summary: A Copper Age culture of Northern Italy's Po Valley (4th–3rd millennium BCE), known for finds of flint axes and copper and arsenical silver weapons.

remedello.name: Remedello
remedello.summary: A small town in the Brescia province of Lombardy, Italy, which lent its name to a prehistoric culture after burials were found there.

konrad-spindler.name: Konrad Spindler
konrad-spindler.summary: Archaeologist who examined the Ötzi discovery and wrote the widely referenced book Der Mann im Eis about it, remaining active in the field until his death in 2005.

lipari.name: Lipari
lipari.summary: The largest of Sicily's Aeolian Islands in the Tyrrhenian Sea, with about 12,800 permanent residents and a population that swells during the summer tourist season.

monte-arci.name: Monte Arci
monte-arci.summary: A volcanic mountain range in Sardinia, Italy, whose abundant obsidian was mined for weapons and tools since prehistoric times and later traded off the island.

rinaldone-culture.name: Rinaldone culture
rinaldone-culture.summary: An Eneolithic culture that spread across northern and central Lazio, southern Tuscany, Marche and Umbria between the 4th and 3rd millennium BC, named after the town of Rinaldone.

gaudo-culture.name: Gaudo culture
gaudo-culture.summary: An Eneolithic culture of Campania, southern Italy, active at the end of the 4th millennium BCE, known mainly through its necropolis of tombs near Paestum.

paestum.name: Paestum
paestum.summary: An ancient Greek city on Italy's Tyrrhenian coast, famous for three well-preserved Doric temples dating from about 550 to 450 BCE.

mondego-river.name: Mondego River
mondego-river.summary: The longest river entirely within Portugal, running 234 kilometres from the Serra da Estrela mountains to the Atlantic Ocean at Figueira da Foz.

national-archaeological-museum-naples.name: National Archaeological Museum of Naples
national-archaeological-museum-naples.summary: A major Italian archaeological museum holding Greek, Roman and Renaissance works, especially Roman artifacts from Pompeii, Stabiae and Herculaneum; known until 1861 as the Royal Bourbon Museum.

coppa-nevigata.name: Coppa Nevigata
coppa-nevigata.summary: Archaeological site on Italy's Apulian coast occupied from the Neolithic through the Bronze Age, notable for early purple dye extraction starting around 1800 BC.

william-hamilton-diplomat.name: William Hamilton
william-hamilton-diplomat.summary: British diplomat, antiquarian and vulcanologist (1730–1803) who served as envoy to the Kingdom of Naples and collected antiquities while studying local volcanoes.
